questions.prompt: With W = 10,000, a reply reserve of 1,000 and headroom of 2,000, why is the threshold 7,000 and not 8,000?
options: Because the reply and the headroom leave only 7,000, which is smaller than 8,000
Because the meter adds 1,000 tokens of framing
Because the threshold is always 70% of the window
questions.explanation: The threshold is the smaller of 80% of the window (8,000) and the window minus both reserves (7,000). Here the reserves win.

questions.prompt: Why does the meter start from the provider's reported usage, not estimate everything?
options: The provider's count is exact, so only the part added since is a guess
Estimating is not allowed by the provider
Usage includes the next reply in advance
The estimate is always larger than the real count
questions.explanation: After each reply the provider reports the exact token count. Only the messages added after that reply need the 4-characters rule.

questions.prompt: Why is the reply's max_tokens subtracted from the window?
options: It is the size of the system prompt
It is a safety margin for estimation errors only
The reply uses the same window as the request
questions.explanation: The provider counts the reply's tokens in the same context window. A request that fills the window leaves no room to answer.
